newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin and ministers meet on French youth jobs law.
newsitem.headline: Jospin and ministers meet on French youth jobs law.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and several ministers met on Tuesday to discuss the drawing up of a draft law on youth employment.

"It was a working meeting...there are still some outstanding issues," government spokesman Catherine Trautmann told reporters after the three-hour meeting on the draft law, which is due to go to cabinet for approval on August 20.
"(Employment Minister) Martine Aubry will provide the details once the final issues have been settled," she added.

The new Socialist-led government has set itself a target of creating 350,000 public sector jobs for young people over the next few years and has promised to push for creation of a similar number of jobs in the private sector.

Defence Minister Alain Richard, who was present at Tuesday's meeting, told reporters the goal of the law would be to ensure that "at the end of 1998 we have at least 150,000 extra jobs for the young in services related to the public interest".
